prs.title: fix(stdio): handle BrokenResourceError in stdout_reader race (#1960)
prs.author: ddullah
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: BrokenResourceError (and ConnectionResetError) raised in stdout_reader when the caller exits the stdio_client context while the subprocess is still writing — the memory stream is already closed but the reader hasn't returned yet. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: BrokenResourceError (and ConnectionResetError) raised in stdout_reader when the caller exits the stdio_client context while the subprocess is still writing — the memory stream is already closed but the reader hasn't returned yet. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2450 wraps each individual read_stream_writer.send() call in its own try/except and returns early, which is the more precise fix: it stops the reader immediately at the point of failure rather than relying on the outer loop catching it. PR #2456 also catches BrokenResourceError, but only at the outer except clause, which still lets the inner sends throw unhandled during a race. Additionally, PR #2456 bundles an unrelated encoding_error_handler default change ('strict' → 'replace') that should be reviewed separately on its own merits.

(2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: UrlElicitationRequiredError is not pickle-safe: default __reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args) = cls(code, message, data), which mismatches the subclass constructor signature (elicitations, message=None), raising TypeError on unpickle (issue #2431). It also adds test coverage in tests/shared/test_exceptions.py and explicitly closes #2431. PR #2478 introduces a _restore_mcp_error dispatcher but the shown diff contains no __reduce__ definition anywhere — the helper is defined but never wired up — making the fix incomplete as presented.

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP client errors (server crash, connection failure, HTTP 4xx/5xx) are not converted to JSONRPCError responses, causing tool calls to hang indefinitely instead of returning a failure to the caller. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2607 wraps the dispatch point for both `_handle_post_request` and `_handle_resumption_request` in a single try/except, giving the broadest exception coverage across both request paths. members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: RequestResponder.cancel() does not comply with the MCP cancellation protocol: it was sending an error response for cancelled requests (forbidden by spec) and failing to send the required notifications/cancelled notification on timeout or caller cancellation. Both PRs modify the same cancel() method to fix this. (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2514 adds the spec-required positive behavior (emitting notifications/cancelled on timeout and caller cancellation) making it the complete fix, whereas #2493 only removes the incorrect error-response sending without substituting the correct notification. #2514's diff is also larger, includes the CancelledNotificationParams import, and covers both the timeout and caller-cancellation paths.
